prompt: You arrive late to the next pub. What’s your first move?
option_a: March up to the lads and tell them to get you a pint.
option_b: Ask if anyone wants something while you’re at the bar.
option_c: Immediately disappear to befriend some random cryptid at the fruit machine.
rationale_correct: Heading straight to the bar and offering to sort drinks is solid mate behaviour.
rationale_wrong: Don’t treat your pals like bar staff or wander off chasing random chaos instead of actually joining your own group.

prompt: You’ve been asked to book the next Christmas Nandos meal. What do you choose?
option_a: The Polish Club.
option_b: Nandos.
option_c: Somewhere five minutes from your house.
rationale_correct: You’ve picked somewhere with proper character for the whole group, not just the easiest option.
rationale_wrong: Don’t phone it in with teenage choices or make everyone travel to your doorstep just to suit yourself.

prompt: Your missus phones. She’s in town and wants to join the night. What’s your move?
option_a: Ask the boys first and see how they feel.
option_b: Irish goodbye and go join her without telling anyone.
option_c: Tell her to just show up without asking the lads.
rationale_correct: Checking with the group first shows you actually value their night too.
rationale_wrong: Ditching the lads or dropping surprise guests on them makes it feel like they were a warm-up act, not your plan.

prompt: Your Secret Santa gift hasn’t arrived in time. What now?
option_a: Just explain you tried and hope they understand.
option_b: Grab a decent last-minute bottle of whisky.
option_c: Pick up a £5 Nandos gift card and call it a day.
rationale_correct: You’ve adapted, put some effort in and made sure nobody is left sitting empty-handed.
rationale_wrong: Doing the bare minimum or nothing at all leaves your mate feeling like an afterthought.

prompt: One of the boys is clearly steaming and wobbling about. What do you do?
option_a: Film him for TikTok and send it to the group chat.
option_b: Steady him, get him some water and make sure he’s alright.
option_c: Pretend you didn’t see anything because you can’t be arsed dealing with it.
rationale_correct: Looking after your mate when he’s burst is peak good-friend behaviour.
rationale_wrong: If your first instinct is content farming or ignoring him, you’ve missed the whole point of being out together.

prompt: The group is choosing the next pub. What do you contribute?
option_a: Say “Anywhere’s fine lads, I don’t care” and offer nothing useful.
option_b: Suggest a decent spot and offer to phone ahead.
option_c: Launch into a rant about how every place in town is terrible now.
rationale_correct: You’re actually helping move the night along and making things easier for everyone.
rationale_wrong: Being useless or relentlessly negative drags the vibe and makes planning harder than it needs to be.

prompt: One of the boys orders a wild, colourful cocktail. What’s your move?
option_a: Absolutely roast him for it in front of everyone.
option_b: Laugh with him and let the man enjoy his ridiculous drink.
option_c: Order the same thing but loudly insist it’s just for the banter.
rationale_correct: Letting your pal enjoy his daft drink without turning it into bullying is the right kind of banter.
rationale_wrong: If you’re more focused on saving face than letting your mate enjoy himself, you’re missing the point.

prompt: Someone suggests doing shots but the lads all look a bit fragile. What do you do?
option_a: Buy ten shots anyway and slam them on the table.
option_b: Read the room and suggest something gentler or skip it.
option_c: Call everyone boring for not being up for it.
rationale_correct: You’re matching the energy of the group instead of forcing carnage on people who clearly aren’t there for it.
rationale_wrong: Forcing shots or shaming people into drinking is tight behaviour, not big-night heroics.

prompt: A mate is telling a long, chaotic story that’s going nowhere. What do you do?
option_a: Walk away mid-sentence.
option_b: Stick with it and let him finish the story.
option_c: Interrupt and hijack the story so it’s about you instead.
rationale_correct: Letting your pal get his nonsense story out is part of the fun of the night.
rationale_wrong: Walking off or stealing the spotlight just says you think you’re more important than the people you’re out with.

prompt: You spot an empty table the group could use. What now?
option_a: Sprint for it like you’re in a game show.
option_b: Point it out and head over together with the lads.
option_c: Hover beside it in silence hoping someone reads your mind.
rationale_correct: You’ve helped secure a base for the group without turning it into some feral competition.
rationale_wrong: Charging solo or acting too awkward to speak just makes everything more chaotic than it needs to be.

prompt: The bar queue is massive. What’s your move?
option_a: Push in like you own the place.
option_b: Wait your turn like a functioning member of society.
option_c: Start loudly moaning to anyone who’ll listen.
rationale_correct: You’re playing fair and not making life harder for the staff or everyone else waiting.
rationale_wrong: Queue-jumping or performative moaning just makes you that guy everyone secretly hates.

prompt: Someone bought a round while you were outside. How do you respond?
option_a: Pretend the round system doesn’t apply to you.
option_b: Offer to grab the next round to even things up.
option_c: Start complaining that it’s unfair you missed out.
rationale_correct: You’ve kept things fair without making a drama out of it.
rationale_wrong: Acting like you’re exempt from rounds or treating them like a court case is tight as anything.

prompt: The lads ask you to take a group photo. What do you do?
option_a: Fire off a blurry horror show and call it done.
option_b: Take a moment to frame it properly so everyone’s actually in it.
option_c: Refuse because you’re ‘terrible with cameras’.
rationale_correct: You’ve helped capture the night properly instead of ruining the memories.
rationale_wrong: Can’t-be-arsed energy or deliberate sabotage just kills everyone’s chance of having a decent photo.

prompt: It’s freezing outside and one of the boys forgot his jacket.
option_a: Mock him for being soft the whole time.
option_b: Get him inside or find a warmer spot for the group.
option_c: Tell him he’ll be fine and carry on as normal.
rationale_correct: You’re looking after the group and not leaving anyone to freeze for the sake of a pint.
rationale_wrong: If your first instinct is slagging or dismissing him, you’re prioritising patter over basic decency.

prompt: The lads are discussing the Secret Santa budget. What’s your input?
option_a: Insist a tenner is more than enough.
option_b: Say you’re happy with whatever works best for everyone.
option_c: Announce how much you spent last year like a martyr.
rationale_correct: You’re keeping it flexible and focused on what suits the group, not your personal agenda.
rationale_wrong: Dragging the budget down or making it all about your generosity kills the fun fast.

prompt: Someone knocks over a pint by accident. What now?
option_a: Laugh at them like it’s the funniest thing you’ve ever seen.
option_b: Help clean it up and sort a replacement drink.
option_c: Kick off about how they’ve ruined the night.
rationale_correct: You’ve handled a minor disaster like a grown-up and kept the night moving.
rationale_wrong: Acting like a spilled pint is either stand-up material or a crisis is way over the top.

prompt: It’s time to move to the next place, but one of the boys has vanished.
option_a: Leave him and hope he respawns later.
option_b: Check the toilets or outside to make sure he’s alright.
option_c: Loudly slag him off for always disappearing.
rationale_correct: Checking on your mate shows you actually give a toss about him getting home alive.
rationale_wrong: Leaving him or turning it into a public moan session is pure useless friend energy.

prompt: One of the lads admits he’s skint tonight.
option_a: Mock him for being brassic.
option_b: Quietly offer to cover a drink or two.
option_c: Announce it loudly so everyone knows.
rationale_correct: You’ve supported your mate without making a big deal of it.
rationale_wrong: Shaming or broadcasting someone’s money situation is deeply shite behaviour.

prompt: You’ve been waiting ages for a taxi. What do you do?
option_a: Spam angry messages to the driver through the app.
option_b: Suggest grabbing a snack or having a laugh while you wait.
option_c: Moan constantly like the universe is personally attacking you.
rationale_correct: You’re keeping spirits up and making the wait part of the night instead of a misery pit.
rationale_wrong: Raging at drivers or subjecting everyone to your monologue of complaints helps absolutely no one.

prompt: The night is winding down. How do you wrap things up?
option_a: Ghost everyone and disappear without a word.
option_b: Say proper goodbyes and check people are getting home safe.
option_c: Insist the night must continue even though everyone is done.
rationale_correct: You’re closing out the night respectfully and making sure people get home in one piece.
rationale_wrong: Vanishing or forcing overtime on shattered people isn’t big-night energy, it’s just inconsiderate.
